root.name: Ruy Lopez: Exchange, Alekhine Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Bxc6 dxc6 5. d4 exd4 6. Qxd4 Qxd4 7. Nxd4 Bd7

overview: A queenless endgame arrives after Bxc6, d4 and Nxd4 with 7...Bd7: White has a healthy 4-vs-3 kingside majority, Black has the bishop pair and doubled c-pawns. White tries to make the majority tell, while Black uses the bishop pair and tries to avoid being squeezed. The game is steady and technical.

white_ideas.idea: Advance the kingside majority and create a passed pawn
Trade the bishops or restrict them with Nc3/Be3
Castle long and use the d-file

black_ideas.idea: Use the bishop pair and activity
Play against the doubled c-pawn weakness
Trade rooks and head for a drawn endgame

typical_structures.structure: White 4v3 kingside majority against Black's doubled c-pawns

character.notes: A technical endgame with no attacks where White squeezes slowly.

structure.notes: Asymmetrical pawns with the d-file open after the queen swap.

approach.notes: A standard Ruy Lopez exchange line.

character.reason: Queens are off, there are no attacks and the position is hard to lose quickly.

gambit.reason: Material is level and no pawn is offered.

soundness.reason: A fully respectable Ruy Lopez line.

structure.reason: An asymmetric pawn structure with the d-file open after the queen swap.

approach.reason: A normal Ruy Lopez main branch.

level.reason: Understanding of the endgame matters more than memorised theory.

plans.reason: Black has the bishop pair and the doubled c-pawn is the structural talking point.
